Investigate treams autodiff without requiring users to import backend-specific treams modules.

This is a separate, non-blocking design investigation requested by the repository owner during release preparation. The release agent continues independently. Do not contact the release agent or wait for release work. Do not implement changes now.

The user's question was: "is it possible to make autodiff work for treams with different autodiff backends with importing specific treams autodiff backends? right now having to do import treams.advect is somewhat unintuitive". Interpret this as asking whether the ordinary treams API can select the appropriate differentiation adapter WITHOUT imports such as import treams.advect, while retaining Advect, JAX, and PyTorch support.

Authoritative source:

  • treams-rs, release/integration at fcf62400700e326ffcc61ec50025cb25ea43ea6d. Recheck the revision, and use git show at that SHA if release work later advances it.
  • advect, currently d5f4bae154f040f1e80c32dc7c1aab41e4c155dc. Recheck the revision and inspect current code rather than assuming old architecture.

Constraints:

  • Read-only investigation. Do not edit either repository, add dependencies, create worktrees, run native builds, change Git refs, commit, push, open issues/PRs, or send external messages.
  • No dependency installation or broad test suites. Small existing-environment probes are fine if they do not rebuild/install anything. Cap CPU threads at 1 for any probe. If relevant environments are unavailable, use source evidence and state the execution gap.
  • Do not modify Codex or user configuration, memories, or agent skills. Do not inspect credentials.
  • Final answer is the durable report; the launcher writes it outside the repository. Include exact source file/line pointers and revision IDs. Do not attempt to write files yourself in the read-only sandbox.
  • Prefer the smallest coherent design. New registries, plugin systems, compatibility layers, elaborate fallback paths, and global state need a concrete reason.
  • Prose must be objective, concise, approachable, and respectful of the reader's time. Explain necessary programming terms briefly. Physics terminology is fine.

Questions to resolve:

  1. What do the existing treams modules and backends actually expose, and what prevents ordinary treams calls from preserving differentiation today? Distinguish Python class methods, ufunc-like functions, raw NumPy operations, and Rust calls. Establish the correct import namespace (treams_rs vs treams) from source.
  2. Can selection by input array/tracer types transparently reuse the existing custom derivative implementations? Cover Advect tracing, JAX tracing and JIT, PyTorch eager and compile, array_ufunc, array_function, array_namespace/Array API. Explain why a protocol is or is not sufficient at the Rust derivative boundary.
  3. How can optional backend imports stay lazy and avoid startup cost/mandatory dependencies? Preserve ordinary NumPy return types and behavior. Identify ambiguity with Python floats/NumPy arrays, zero differentiable inputs, nested containers, constructors and materials, constants, mixed backend values, tracing-context detection, and accidental array coercions.
  4. Compare a small transparent dispatch boundary with one explicit backend/context choice and the existing modules. Recommend the smallest useful supported scope. Do not imply a universal implementation is already present.
  5. Provide a short proposed user-facing API example that can be run after implementation, clearly labeled as a proposal; separately show an existing runnable equivalent where possible. Include realistic gradients/parameters rather than invented function names. State JIT/compile/higher-order/device limits based on current adapters.
  6. Outline the minimal implementation locations and meaningful validation needed for a later change, including output/cotangent conventions and performance of ordinary NumPy calls. No implementation in this investigation.

Check current official library documentation if needed for changing or uncertain external API claims. Use primary sources only and cite exact pages. Local repository source is authoritative for project-specific behavior. […]

Deliver a concise decision first, then evidence, alternatives/tradeoffs, and a bounded follow-up plan. Clearly separate source-confirmed facts, inferences, and behavior not executed. This report must not create a release blocker.

The adapters already provide the Rust derivative connection needed for automatic selection. Their current limits would remain: CPU and first-order gradients, JAX JIT supported, and PyTorch compile unsupported. I also confirmed that treams_rs.advect can already be accessed lazily after importing only treams_rs; that avoids a separate import, though it still requires an explicit choice.
